classification.habit: Large perennial herbaceous plant; commercial drug is an oleo-gum-resin
classification.habitat: Dry mountainous regions; the resin is obtained from Ferula species cultivated or collected mainly in Southwest/Central Asia
classification.distribution: The crude asafoetida drug is largely obtained through cultivation and trade from Iran, Afghanistan and neighbouring regions; Ferula taxonomy in commerce requires authentication

identification.description: Hingu is a dried oleo-gum-resin drug with a characteristic strong odour; the botanical source is a Ferula species and the resin is obtained from underground parts.
identification.whole_plant: Ferula plants are tall perennial herbs with a robust basal rosette and a large flowering stem; the traded drug is usually resin rather than the intact plant.
identification.root: Large taproot/rootstock from which the oleo-gum-resin is obtained by incision in source material.
identification.stem: Mature Ferula species have a tall, hollow or solid flowering stem with sheathing leaf bases.
identification.leaf: Large divided basal leaves; exact morphology varies among Ferula species used in commerce.
identification.flower: Small flowers arranged in compound umbels, typical of Apiaceae.
identification.fruit: Dry schizocarp characteristic of Apiaceae; not normally the traded medicinal part.
identification.seed: Flattened ridged mericarps typical of the genus; source-species authentication is important.
identification.bark: Not applicable as a distinct medicinal bark character.
identification_points: Ferula-type large divided leaves and umbels

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Asafoetida contains resin, gum and volatile components; composition varies with source and processing. Exact marker compounds should be taken from an authenticated pharmacopoeial monograph rather than inferred from common food descriptions.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Asafoetida is widely used as a culinary spice and traditional digestive aromatic. Modern pharmacological findings are heterogeneous and should not be presented as established clinical efficacy for a specific disorder.
modern_information.safety_notes: Use appropriate food/pharmacopoeial quality material. Strongly concentrated resin should not be treated as equivalent to culinary quantities.

exam_points: Botanical source recorded as Ferula assa-foetida L.
viva_questions: What is the botanical source of Hingu in this record?
Which family does Hingu belong to?
What is the traded medicinal part?
Why is botanical authentication important for Hingu?
identification_points: Not a bark or leaf drug
mnemonics: Hingu = Hing: pungent resin from Ferula of Apiaceae.
student.quick_revision: Hingu is an oleo-gum-resin drug associated with Ferula and Apiaceae; the project record describes it as Katu, Laghu-Snigdha-Tikshna and Ushna.

teaching_points: Explain crude-drug identification of an oleo-gum-resin versus a whole plant.
Demonstrate Apiaceae/Ferula source and the importance of species authentication.
discussion_points: Difference between culinary asafoetida and pharmacopoeial crude drug
practical_points: Observe colour, texture and characteristic odour of authenticated material.
Do not infer source species from odour alone; verify supplier and pharmacopoeial identity.

doctor.quick_reference: Hingu — Ferula assa-foetida L. in the project record; useful part is oleo-gum-resin and traditional indications centre on digestive/Vata-related presentations.
key_precautions: Verify source species and quality of resin.
Do not derive therapeutic dosing from culinary use.
Use authoritative references for dose, formulation and contraindications.
